title: AVO-7 – Part 5
description: Compass systems, directional gyros, flux valves, magnetic heading systems, and inertial reference systems.

questions.question: How to correct the heading when the flux detector malfunctions or is manually disconnected?
options: Pilot manually sets the north reference on the ground by DG (Directional Gyro) by reading from the magnetic compass.
Pilot resets the heading automatically using GPS only.
Pilot uses the pitot-static system to establish magnetic heading.
questions.explanation: The heading can be manually referenced to magnetic north using the magnetic compass and directional gyro.

questions.question: What is the drift due to Earth rate on the north gyro stabilized INS when the aircraft is flying at 90° latitude?
questions.explanation: Earth-rate drift for a north gyro is 15° × cos(latitude). At 90°, cos(90°) = 0, giving 0°/hr.

questions.question: What is the drift due to Earth rate on north gyro stabilized INS when the A/C is flying at 0° latitude?
questions.explanation: At 0° latitude, 15° × cos(0°) = 15°/hr.

questions.question: Which one of the following excitation current is used with flux valves?
questions.explanation: The flux valve uses AC excitation in its primary coil.

questions.question: On the pneumatic driven directional gyro, how is a heading presented with the whole gimbal assembly being fixed and the case moving along with the aircraft's heading?
options: Heading is indicated relative to the fixed gimbal system as the case rotates around it.
Heading is indicated only by the magnetic compass.
Heading is calculated from pitot pressure.
questions.explanation: The fixed gimbal provides the reference while the case rotates with aircraft heading.

questions.question: What is magnetic declination?
options: The vertical angle between the aircraft and Earth.
The horizontal angle contained between the true and magnetic meridian at any place.
The difference between aircraft pitch and roll.
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the true and magnetic meridians.

questions.question: The slave torque motor on a remote electrical directional gyro is used to...
options: Precess the gyro using heading data from the flux valve.
questions.explanation: The slaving system uses heading information from the flux valve to drive the slaving torque motor and precess the gyro.

questions.question: Drift due to Earth rate on the vertical gyro at zero-degree latitude?
questions.explanation: Vertical gyro Earth-rate drift is 15° × sin(latitude). At 0°, the result is 0°/hr.

questions.question: One reason for swinging a compass:
options: After cockpit modification or major replacement involving ferrous metal.
questions.explanation: Compass swinging is performed when aircraft magnetic characteristics may have changed, such as after modifications involving ferrous material.

questions.question: System that uses a strapdown platform attached to the airframe:
questions.explanation: Modern inertial systems can use strapdown configurations attached directly to the aircraft structure.

questions.question: Erection mechanism utilizes gyro property
questions.explanation: Gyro erection systems use the principle of precession to return the gyro to its reference position.

questions.question: DG provides
questions.explanation: A directional gyro provides a stable short-term heading reference but requires correction for drift.

questions.question: Lighting bulb wire
options: Twisting and grounding the wires from the compass case
questions.explanation: The compass lighting wiring is arranged by twisting and grounding the wires from the compass case.

questions.question: Magnetic compass bowls are fitted with liquid to
questions.explanation: The liquid dampens movement and oscillation of the compass float and magnets.

questions.question: While working on and around flux valve
options: Use non-magnetic tools when working within 3 feet
Place a strong magnetic field near the valve
questions.explanation: Non-magnetic tools are required near the flux valve to prevent magnetic interference.

questions.question: At what time after power is removed gyro rotor stops
questions.explanation: The gyro rotor may continue spinning after power removal; maintenance procedures specify waiting about 3 minutes.

questions.question: Which one uses the laser gyro
questions.explanation: Laser gyros are used as inertial sensors in modern inertial reference systems.

questions.question: What is main function of electrical connector at the back of magnetic compass
questions.explanation: The electrical connector supplies the compass illumination circuit.

questions.question: When A/C descent and bank, the indicator gives false reading because of
questions.explanation: Pitch and roll can produce gimbal errors that cause false indications.

questions.question: Purpose of magnetic compass
options: To indicate heading with respect to magnetic north
questions.explanation: The magnetic compass provides aircraft heading referenced to magnetic north.

questions.question: Vertical component of magnetic field around equator
questions.explanation: Near the magnetic equator, the vertical component of Earth's magnetic field is approximately zero.

questions.question: Purpose of degaussing
questions.explanation: Degaussing removes residual magnetism from aircraft structures and components.

questions.question: Action should be taken before degaussing standby compass area
options: Open the compass lighting circuit breaker
questions.explanation: The compass lighting circuit breaker should be opened before degaussing the standby compass area.

questions.question: What is magnetic declination?
options: The vertical change between aircraft pitch and roll.
The horizontal change contained between the true and magnetic meridian at any place
The difference between indicated and true airspeed.
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angular relationship between true and magnetic meridians.

questions.question: Components of flux detector
options: Spokes, collector horns, primary and secondary coil
Pitot tube, static port, drain valve
questions.explanation: The flux detector contains spokes, collector horns, and primary and secondary coils.

questions.question: When Inertial Reference System (IRS) is on battery, the indication is
options: ON BATTERY light indication and horn sound
questions.explanation: Battery operation is indicated by the ON BATTERY indication and an audible horn.

questions.question: What data is displayed on Radio Magnetic Indicator?
options: Magnetic heading and magnetic bearing of an aircraft with reference to ground-based transmitting stations of radio navigation systems
questions.explanation: The RMI combines magnetic heading information with bearing information from radio navigation sources.

questions.question: On radio magnetic indicator, magnetic heading data is displayed by
questions.explanation: The rotating heading card provides the magnetic heading reference.

questions.question: Which of the following is the error of directional gyro?
questions.explanation: Directional gyroscopes experience drift, which must be corrected by an erection or slaving system.

questions.question: Operating an aircraft near the magnetic poles causes what is known as
questions.explanation: The steep angle of Earth's magnetic field near the poles produces dip-related compass errors.

questions.question: What is the cause of gyro nutation?
options: Low rotational speed and gyro gimbal ring axes are not mutually perpendicular
questions.explanation: Gyro nutation can occur due to low rotational speed and improper perpendicularity of the gimbal axes.

questions.question: The magnetic flux passing through flux detector coil is maximum when it is ___ degree with the direction of the earth's magnetic field degree with the...
questions.explanation: Flux is maximum when the coil/spoke is parallel to the magnetic field, corresponding to 0°.

questions.question: When a warning flag of a related directional gyro on an indicator is view, what is the possible correction action?
questions.explanation: Checking or resetting the related circuit breaker is a possible corrective action for the indicated DG warning.

questions.question: The effects of deviation due to longitudinal and lateral components of aircraft magnetism are compensated by
questions.explanation: Compensating magnets are used to counteract aircraft magnetic effects that produce compass deviation.

questions.question: A better solution to deviation error is to remotely locate the magnetic compass in
options: A wing tip or vertical stabilizer
questions.explanation: Locating the magnetic sensing element away from magnetic interference, such as at a wing tip or vertical stabilizer, reduces deviation.

questions.question: What is the info provided by inertial reference system?
questions.explanation: The IRS provides navigation information such as aircraft heading, position, and velocity.

questions.question: What will be the output data when the acceleration data is supplied to a primary stage integrator?
questions.explanation: Integrating acceleration with respect to time gives velocity or ground speed.

questions.question: Which one of the following reference indicates the heading reference?
questions.explanation: The compass card provides the heading reference.

questions.question: Which one of the following torque motor used in mercury leveling switch?
questions.explanation: The leveling torque motor is associated with the mercury leveling switch system.

questions.question: INS stabilized in horizontal position in attitude change b/c
options: It doesn't have a third accelerometer to correct vertical movement
It uses the pitot system to control attitude
questions.explanation: The supplied material states that the horizontal stabilization is related to the absence of a third accelerometer for vertical movement correction.

questions.question: To eliminate reverse reading of compass card
questions.explanation: Horizontal presentation is used to eliminate reverse reading of the compass card.

questions.question: Compass bowl is made up of
questions.explanation: The compass bowl is made from non-magnetic material to avoid interference with the magnetic sensing system.

questions.question: On which one of the following types of magnetic heading references do the compass card rotate opposite to the direction of the intended turn?
questions.explanation: The supplied material identifies the vertical magnetic compass as having this compass-card movement characteristic.

questions.question: What is the drift due to earth rate on the vertical gyro stabilized INS when the aircraft is flying on 90° latitude?
questions.explanation: Vertical gyro Earth-rate drift is 15° × sin(latitude). At 90°, sin(90°) = 1, giving 15°/hr.

questions.question: Through which one of the following components is the excitation current supplied to the flux valve?
questions.explanation: AC excitation is supplied through the primary coil of the flux valve.

questions.question: When initializing inertial reference system (IRS)
questions.explanation: The aircraft must remain stationary during IRS initialization so the system can establish its reference accurately.

questions.question: Which one is means of controlling drift on directional gyroscopes?
questions.explanation: Erection devices correct gyro drift and maintain the required reference.

questions.question: What does pulling of the caging knob do to the directional gyroscope?
options: Disconnecting the outer gimbal from the rigid inner gimbal and rotor
questions.explanation: Pulling the caging knob releases or disconnects the outer gimbal arrangement as specified in the source.

questions.question: Which one of the following is correct when degaussing the windshield area of the cockpit on B-737 aircraft?
options: Move the AC demagnetizing coil slowly towards windshield areas, bring the AC demagnetizing coil as close as possible to the structure without touching the structure.
Place the coil directly against the windshield and hold it stationary.
Use a permanent magnet directly on the windshield.
questions.explanation: The AC demagnetizing coil is moved slowly toward the area and kept as close as possible without touching the structure.

questions.question: A card on a directional gyro is installed on
questions.explanation: The directional gyro card is mounted on the outer ring.

questions.question: The position data for IRS initialization can be obtained
options: Automatically from GPS or entered manually
questions.explanation: Initial position may be supplied automatically by GPS or entered manually.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a line drawn on an aeronautical chart that connects the location on the planet where a compass pointing to magnetic north is also pointing to geographic True North?
questions.explanation: An agonic line connects points where magnetic variation is zero.

questions.question: Which one of the following lines on aeronautical charts indicates points of equal variation?
questions.explanation: Isogonic lines connect points having equal magnetic variation.

questions.question: The variation of compass liquid volume is compensated by
questions.explanation: A bellows expansion unit accommodates changes in compass liquid volume caused by temperature.

questions.question: The property of magnetic compass liquid is
questions.explanation: Compass liquid must have a low freezing point so it remains usable at low temperatures.

questions.question: ILS info is displayed on
questions.explanation: ILS course and glide-slope information can be displayed on the CDI.

questions.question: Where is flux detector element located on an aircraft?
questions.explanation: Flux detector elements are remotely located at areas such as wing tips or vertical stabilizers to reduce magnetic interference.

questions.question: A knob on a directional gyro used to set it to indicate the same heading as the magnetic compass is
questions.explanation: The caging/heading-setting knob is used to set the DG indication to the required heading reference.

questions.question: Directional gyro employs
questions.explanation: The directional gyro uses a horizontal-axis gyroscope to maintain directional reference.

questions.question: Where is flux valve located on an aircraft?
questions.explanation: The flux valve is normally located at a remote wing-tip position to minimize magnetic interference.

questions.question: The erection system used for pneumatic directional gyro is
options: Air reaction off the wedge plate
questions.explanation: The pneumatic directional gyro uses air reaction from the wedge plate as its erection mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about remote-indicating compasses system?
options: A magnetic detecting element monitors a gyroscopic indicating element
A pitot probe directly drives the compass card
A fuel probe controls the gyro
questions.explanation: The remote compass system uses a magnetic detecting element to provide magnetic reference information to the gyroscopic indicating system.

questions.question: Which of the following is the remote indication system of gyro output from flux valve?
options: Slaving servo amplifier to slaving torque motor
questions.explanation: The slaving servo amplifier processes the error and drives the slaving torque motor.

questions.question: Caging and heading setting knob
options: Hold inner ring gimbal and rotor while rotating outer gimbal
questions.explanation: The caging and heading-setting mechanism holds the inner gimbal and rotor while the outer gimbal is positioned.

questions.question: Pneumatic operated DG, magnetic bearing indication provided using
questions.explanation: The pneumatic DG uses concentrically mounted pointers to provide magnetic bearing indication.

questions.question: The procedure of correcting the indication of deviation error is minimized by two small permanent magnets inside the compensating mechanism in the compass
questions.explanation: Compass swinging is the procedure used to determine and minimize deviation using the compass compensating mechanism.

questions.question: Magnetic compass error
options: Magnetic variation, magnetic deviation, dip error
Pitot error, static error, fuel error
Engine error, hydraulic error, electrical error
questions.explanation: The supplied material identifies variation, deviation, and dip as magnetic compass errors.

questions.question: The effects of deviation due to longitudinal and lateral components of aircraft magnetism are compensated by
questions.explanation: Compass compensating devices reduce deviation caused by aircraft magnetism.

questions.question: Output data from the 2nd integrator gives
questions.explanation: Integrating acceleration once gives velocity/ground speed; integrating again gives distance or position.

questions.question: What does an IRS require to give the aircraft's current position?
questions.explanation: The IRS requires an initial position reference before it can calculate the aircraft's subsequent position.

questions.question: What should be the possible correction action for leaking magnetic compass?
questions.explanation: A leaking magnetic compass should be replaced according to the supplied maintenance information.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about compass bowl?
options: It is made from non-magnetic material.
It can be made from magnetic material
questions.explanation: The compass bowl should not be made from magnetic material because it could interfere with compass operation.

questions.question: The floating magnets in a compass are not affected by
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies plastic materials as not affecting the floating magnets magnetically.

questions.question: One of the oldest and simplest instruments for indicating direction is
questions.explanation: The magnetic compass is one of the oldest and simplest instruments used for indicating direction.

questions.question: Which component of the directional gyro is stationary?
questions.explanation: The housing or outer case is the stationary part of the directional gyro.

questions.question: Which one of the inertial position determining systems uses gimbaled gyroscope for their operation?
questions.explanation: A conventional INS can use gimbaled gyroscopes to maintain the inertial reference platform.

questions.question: At which one of the following latitudes does an operational inertial navigation unit or an inertial reference unit take a longer time to align?
questions.explanation: Alignment takes longer at higher latitudes because of the characteristics of Earth-rate sensing and inertial alignment.

questions.question: For one detector spoke, how many headings correspond to zero flux?
questions.explanation: For one detector spoke, two headings correspond to zero flux because the magnetic-field relationship repeats in opposite directions.

questions.question: How many accelerometers are used in IRS strapdowns?
questions.explanation: A strapdown IRS uses three accelerometers to measure acceleration along the three aircraft axes.

questions.question: The brake is also applied approximately __ seconds after the power supply has been switched off to prevent spinning of the gyroscope about its vertical axis during rundown
questions.explanation: The supplied maintenance information specifies approximately 30 seconds after power removal for brake application.

questions.question: Accelerometer used for the longitudinal axis
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the North-South accelerometer for the longitudinal axis.

questions.question: All A/C heading detected using
questions.explanation: The flux detector uses three spokes arranged to sense the Earth's magnetic field and determine aircraft heading.

questions.question: Spoke detector made of
questions.explanation: The flux detector spokes are made of Permalloy, a material suitable for sensing magnetic flux.
